topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the core learning objectives concerning cancer treatment approaches and their mechanisms of action.

topics.label: Conventional Cancer Treatments: Surgery, Radiotherapy, and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain standard modalities of cancer treatment—including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapeutic agents—along with their systemic toxicities and mechanisms of drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting Intrinsic Cancer Cell Vulnerabilities and Checkpoint Defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that selectively exploit cancer-specific biological vulnerabilities, including hormone dependencies, cell cycle checkpoint deficiencies, oncolytic viral selectivity, and synthetic lethality in DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Oncogene Addiction and Kinase Inhibitor Therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on targeting driver mutations through small-molecule kinase inhibitors, detailing their therapeutic mechanism, the emergence of gatekeeper mutations and bypass resistance, and dosing strategies.

topics.label: Therapeutic Monoclonal Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the design and mechanisms of antibody-based therapies used to block surface receptors, recruit immune effector responses, and deliver targeted cytotoxic payloads to cancer cells.

topics.label: Cancer Immunotherapy and T-Cell-Directed Therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biological principles and clinical applications of mobilizing host immunity against tumors, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, neoantigen recognition, bispecific T-cell engagers, and CAR T-cell therapies.

topics.label: Current Challenges, Historical Progress, and Future Directions in Cancer Therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize the clinical challenges of tumor heterogeneity and trial design with historical improvements in cancer survival and prospective strategies in early detection, cancer vaccines, and personalised medicine.
